cloudflareSameTabObservation.captureScoringScope: Direct scrapePage/evaluate captures: adapter API status 200 denotes a completed direct function, not a separately observed browser-service or Firecrawl API HTTP response. Initial and final captures share four document visits.

findings: Cloudflare success text was hidden template content, not evidence of completed verification. In the live Zoopla observation Chromium was already allowed, while Firefox remained on HTTP 403 after more than ten seconds; no delayed recovery was observed.

Changing process/browser timezone from UTC to Vietnam time added no selected normalized matches: Chromium 7/16 versus 6/16, Firefox 5/16 versus 4/16. Main-thread and worker offsets were verified as 0 versus -420 minutes. This does not establish that UTC is universally preferable.

The same pinned Rebrowser driver retrieved 5/14 in the Linux container and 4/14 in each native macOS Chromium/Google Chrome bundle. Native bundles used the Apple M4 Pro GPU, while the container used SwiftShader; all three had the same public egress IP. Neither native bundle added an exclusive match.
The extra container match was the public LinkedIn company page. Roblox timed out on all three platform bundles; native hardware/branding did not resolve that selected failure.
decision: Keep the existing deployment and readiness defaults. No blanket Cloudflare wait, hard-coded Vietnam timezone or native-browser migration is supported by these selected observations.
limits: Live cohorts and resource enforcement differ; these are selected experiments, not a stable vendor rate, causal GPU/OS result, full API rate or hosted parity.
The current source-pinned full API result remains 55/100; earlier actual hosted 81/100 was not refreshed.
A hidden success message cannot establish clearance. Missing/blank frame controls do not establish that a challenge is noninteractive.
Native Chrome used a different patch version and proprietary bundle from bundled Chromium; browser version telemetry does not pin every installed framework/resource byte.
